original.target_description: Experiment 1, Hypothesis 1a: low ($0.50) versus medium ($5.00) cash payment on expected willingness of other students to help load a sofa into a van; planned contrast within the full seven-condition between-participants ANOVA.

n.location: p. 789 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1 Method; Results footnote 3
n.quote: Six hundred fourteen students at the University of California, Berkeley, and Massachusetts Institute of Technology were approached in a variety of campus locations and asked to complete a brief survey.
n.sample_role: Student participants in the full seven-condition ANOVA underlying the planned contrast; cash-condition-specific sample sizes not printed.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported; printed total agrees with the seven-condition model residual df 607.

replication.target_description: Study 1, H1a: low-cash versus medium-cash conditions on expected willingness to help load a sofa into a van; planned estimated-marginal-means comparison in the six-condition between-subject ANOVA, Tukey-adjusted p.

n.sample_role: Participants in the six-cell fitted ANOVA model underlying the H1a estimated-marginal-means contrast; cash pair alone comprises 547 participants.
n.exclusions: No data exclusions; the two nonpayment control conditions are outside this six-cell model.
n.location: Study Designs; Study 1 Results, Replication (paragraphs preceding and following Table 4); Table 4 H1a, Study 1 (assigned p.5 locator). No supplied PDF for layout verification.
n.quote: Our studies followed a 3 (payment form: cash vs. candy vs. monetized candy) x 2 (payment level: small vs. medium) design. ... In Study 1, we employed a between-subject design, similar to the original study. ... Following our pre-registration, no data exclusion was performed. ... We first conducted a 3 (payment form: cash vs. candy vs. monetized candy) x 2 (payment level: low vs. medium) between-subject ANOVA on the expected willingness to help ... We conducted planned pairwise comparisons using estimated marginal means to directly address H1a and H1b (see Tables 4 and 5). ... We found support for H1a, revealing that the expected willingness to help in the medium-cash condition (M = 7.15, SD = 2.60, N = 274) was higher than that in the low-cash condition (M = 3.63, SD = 3.02, N = 273) ... low-candy (M = 5.14, SD = 2.74, N = 275) and medium-candy conditions (M = 6.31, SD = 2.66, N = 276) ... To address H2, we looked at the post hoc comparisons from the 3 x 2 ANOVA and found that the expected willingness to help in the medium monetized candy condition (M = 5.86, SD = 3.00, N = 274) was higher than that in the low monetized candy condition (M = 4.75, SD = 3.02, N = 277, see Tables 4 and 5).

notes:
The study label 1a is matched to Hypothesis 1a (cash payment level) in original Experiment 1 and replication Study 1 using the supplied p. 3 and Table 4 locators. Original F and p retained exactly as printed despite their apparent inconsistency; no p recalculation or effect-size conversion performed. PDF text renders the original equals sign as 5. Replication d is the printed low-minus-medium contrast. Replication Table 4 also supplies a calculated original d; this was not substituted for the statistic printed in the original paper. Replication condition sample sizes are retained separately as printed, rather than substituting the full recruited N.
